fn tri(n: Int) -> Int
  requires (n >= 0)
  ensures (result == (if (n == 1) then 3 else if ((n % 2) == 0) then (1 + (n / 2)) else ((tri((n - 1)) + tri((n - 2))) + tri((n + 1)))))
  ensures (result >= 0)
  effects pure
  example (tri(0) == 1)
  example (tri(1) == 3)

fn Tribonacci(n: Int) -> List[Int]
  requires (n >= 0)
  ensures (len(result) == (n + 1))
  ensures forall i in 0..(n + 1): (result[i] == tri(i))
  ensures forall x in result: (x >= 0)
  effects pure
  example (Tribonacci(0) == [])
